🎯This Lesson’s Objectives▼ Expand
❓
Big Question
Today’s Wonder

A kingdom that stood for years comes apart in a single chapter. How can choices that each seem small add up to something that large?

🎯
Objectives
By the end of this lesson…
🔗Cause and effect: I will follow one chain of events through the chapter, from a secret plot to a crown taken.
📖Reading: I will read Book Four, Chapter 2 and tell what each person chooses when loyalty is tested.
🔤Words: I will learn five words from the chapter.
✉️Letters: I will read seven sealed letters, find who wrote each, and judge whether its promise or warning was kept, broken or unheeded.
📝Writing: I will think about loyalty and trust in writing, using details from the chapter.
📕 You’ll need your copy

cause and effect noun
A cause is why something happens. An effect is what happens because of it.
📌 A chain
One effect can become the cause of the next thing, like a row of falling dominoes.

The Passing of Arthur
Alfred, Lord Tennyson (1869), from Idylls of the King
Then spake King Arthur to Sir Bedivere: “The sequel of today unsolders all The goodliest fellowship of famous knights Whereof this world holds record. Such a sleep They sleep—the men I loved. I think that we Shall never more, at any future time, Delight our souls with talk of knightly deeds, Walking about the gardens and the halls Of Camelot, as in the days that were. I perish by this people which I made,— Though Merlin sware that I should come again To rule once more; but, let what will be, be, I am so deeply smitten through the helm That without help I cannot last till morn.
sequel: what comes after; the result · goodliest: finest · whereof: of which · I perish by this people which I made: I am destroyed by the very people I made into a kingdom · sware: swore, promised · let what will be, be: whatever happens, let it happen · smitten: struck · helm: helmet · morn: morning

✉️ Before Chapter 2
What you need to know from the chapter you skip
Professor Lovelore Before you read
0:30
An AI-generated character and voice.
Book Four begins with a chapter called Launcelot and Guinevere. You do not need to read it.
Sir Launcelot loves Queen Guinevere, King Arthur’s wife, and she loves him.
When a knight carries the queen away, Launcelot rescues her.
Agravain hears the queen ask Launcelot to meet her in her garden. He tells Mordred, who sees his chance, and the two hide there.

Professor Lovelore

Your answer
Professor Lovelore

Well done. Now look at the whole chapter as a chain. Two knights plot against Launcelot. Launcelot is caught, and he escapes. The queen is condemned, and he rescues her. In the rescue, Gawain loses his brothers, and he will not forgive. War follows, and while the king is away, Mordred takes his crown. Each effect becomes the next cause. That is cause and effect.

Professor Lovelore Before you write
0:12
An AI-generated character and voice.

Type your answers here. Everything you type this week is saved and gathered into one Week 5 Work PDF at the end of the fourth lesson. Today, three questions about Chapter 2.

Part 1Chapter ThinkingComplete sentences, with details from the text.
1. Bors begs Launcelot not to go to the queen that night. What does Bors fear, and what does Launcelot’s answer show about him?
2. At first Gawain pardons Launcelot for Agravain’s death. By the time of the siege he refuses every peace. What changed his mind, and why can he not forgive it?
3. Arthur trusts Mordred to rule Britain while he is away. Name two things Mordred does with that trust.
